newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO says food supply deteriorating in Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: FAO says food supply deteriorating in Sierra Leone.

text.p: Sierra Leone will need substantial food aid after a coup last month, the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Monday.

The Rome-based agency said in a news alert that supply was tight as most shops and markets in the West African country remained closed after a violent coup on May 25 by rebel army leader Johnny Paul Koroma.
"The food supply is tightening in the main towns. The price of rice has tripled in (the capital) Freetown and the supply of food and water is deteriorating," it said.
Although some 21,000 tonnes of emergency food aid was available in Sierra Leone, FAO estimated the country would need food imports of 80,000 tonnes this year.
"With the current upheaval, import and food aid requirements will increase significantly," it said.
"Insecurity is severely hampering agricultural activities, especially the planting of the main crop which normally takes place in April to June," FAO said.

The World Food Programme (WFP), which runs United Nations food aid programmes, launched a $19.4 million operation for Sierra Leone early this year to encourage the resettlement of thousands of people displaced by six years of civil war.

Looters pillaged WFP food warehouses in Freetown during last month's coup, stealing 1,650 tonnes of aid provided by the operation. FAO said the renewed unrest had dashed earlier hopes of an improved food situation.

"Contrary to previous expectations following the return to peace, planted areas are likely to be sharply reduced as some farmers will abandon their farms while others are discouraged from cultivating larger areas," FAO said.
